stem: In Matthew 13:18–23, Jesus explains his parable of the sower to the disciples. What does the seed stand for?
options: the prophets sent to Israel
the prayers offered to God
the word of the kingdom
the miracles done in Galilee
why: Matthew 13:19: when anyone hears "the word of the kingdom" and does not understand it, the wicked one snatches it away; the kinds of ground are kinds of hearers, and the good ground hears, understands and bears fruit.

es.stem: En Mateo 13:18–23, Jesús les explica a los discípulos su parábola del sembrador. ¿Qué representa la semilla?
options: los profetas enviados a Israel
las oraciones ofrecidas a Dios
la palabra del reino
los milagros hechos en Galilea
es.why: Mateo 13:19: cuando alguien oye "la palabra del reino" y no la entiende, viene el maligno y se la arrebata; los tipos de tierra son tipos de oyentes, y la buena tierra oye, entiende y da fruto.

stem: In Luke 2, which devout old man takes the infant Jesus in his arms in the temple and prays, "Lord, now lettest thou thy servant depart in peace" (the Nunc dimittis)?
options: Simeon
Zacharias
Nicodemus
Barnabas
why: Luke 2:25–32: Simeon, just and devout, had been promised by the Holy Spirit that he would see the Lord's Christ before he died; he takes the child in his arms and blesses God. His song is sung at evening and night prayer across the churches.

es.stem: En Lucas 2, ¿qué anciano piadoso toma en brazos al niño Jesús en el templo y ora: "Ahora, Señor, despides a tu siervo en paz" (el Nunc dimittis)?
options: Simeón
Zacarías
Nicodemo
Bernabé
es.why: Lucas 2:25–32: a Simeón, justo y piadoso, el Espíritu Santo le había revelado que no moriría sin ver al Cristo del Señor; toma al niño en brazos y bendice a Dios. Su cántico se canta en la oración de la tarde y de la noche en muchas iglesias.

stem: A volunteer who joins a project in its last week receives the same thank-you gift as those who served all year, and the long-serving volunteers grumble. Which parable of Jesus in Matthew's Gospel has the same shape?
options: the ten bridesmaids and their lamps
the servant who would not forgive
the servants and their talents
the workers in the vineyard
why: Matthew 20:1–16: workers hired at the eleventh hour receive a denarius, the same as those who bore the heat of the day; the first-hired grumble, and the owner asks, "is thine eye evil, because I am good?"

es.stem: Un voluntario que se suma a un proyecto en su última semana recibe el mismo regalo de agradecimiento que quienes sirvieron todo el año, y los voluntarios de siempre se quejan. ¿Qué parábola de Jesús en el Evangelio de Mateo tiene la misma forma?
options: las diez vírgenes y sus lámparas
el siervo que no quiso perdonar
los siervos y sus talentos
los obreros de la viña
es.why: Mateo 20:1–16: los obreros contratados a la hora undécima reciben un denario, lo mismo que quienes soportaron el calor del día; los primeros se quejan, y el dueño pregunta: "¿O tienes envidia porque yo soy bueno?"

stem: In Jesus's parable of the Pharisee and the tax collector (Luke 18:9–14), which man goes home justified, and why?
options: the Pharisee, because his fasting and tithing were real
the tax collector, who asks God's mercy as a sinner
the Pharisee, because he opens his prayer with thanks
the tax collector, who vows to repay all he has taken
why: Luke 18:13–14: the tax collector, standing far off, prays "God be merciful to me a sinner," and Jesus says he went home justified rather than the Pharisee, for whoever exalts himself will be humbled.

es.stem: En la parábola de Jesús del fariseo y el publicano (Lucas 18:9–14), ¿cuál de los dos vuelve a casa justificado, y por qué?
options: el fariseo, porque su ayuno y su diezmo eran reales
el publicano, que pide a Dios compasión como pecador
el fariseo, porque comienza su oración dando gracias
el publicano, que promete devolver todo lo que tomó
es.why: Lucas 18:13–14: el publicano, de pie a lo lejos, ora "Dios, ten compasión de mí, que soy pecador", y Jesús dice que este volvió a su casa justificado y no el otro, porque el que se enaltece será humillado.

stem: In Matthew 16, after Peter says, "Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God," what does Jesus say he will give Peter?
options: a seat at his right hand in his kingdom
a sword to defend the coming kingdom
the keys of the kingdom of heaven
a double portion of his own spirit
why: Matthew 16:18–19: Jesus calls Simon Peter the rock on which he will build his church, and says, "I will give unto thee the keys of the kingdom of heaven." Churches read the rock and the keys in different ways; the promise itself is in the text.

es.stem: En Mateo 16, después de que Pedro dice: "Tú eres el Cristo, el Hijo del Dios viviente", ¿qué dice Jesús que le dará a Pedro?
options: un lugar a su derecha en su reino
una espada para defender el reino
las llaves del reino de los cielos
una doble porción de su propio espíritu
es.why: Mateo 16:18–19: Jesús llama a Simón Pedro la roca sobre la que edificará su iglesia, y le dice: "A ti te daré las llaves del reino de los cielos". Las iglesias leen la roca y las llaves de distintas maneras; la promesa misma está en el texto.

stem: In Acts 10, after his vision of a sheet full of unclean animals and his visit to the Roman centurion Cornelius, what does Peter conclude?
options: that God shows no favoritism between peoples
that Cornelius must be circumcised before baptism
that only the apostles may share meals with Gentiles
that he must leave Judea and go to preach in Rome
why: Acts 10:28, 34–35: Peter says God has shown him not to call any person common or unclean, and "God is no respecter of persons"; the Holy Spirit falls on Cornelius's household and Peter has them baptized.

es.stem: En Hechos 10, después de su visión de un lienzo lleno de animales impuros y de su visita al centurión romano Cornelio, ¿a qué conclusión llega Pedro?
options: que Dios no hace distinción entre los pueblos
que Cornelio debe circuncidarse antes del bautismo
que solo los apóstoles pueden comer con gentiles
que debe dejar Judea e ir a predicar a Roma
es.why: Hechos 10:28, 34–35: Pedro dice que Dios le ha mostrado que no llame común o impuro a nadie, y que "Dios no hace acepción de personas"; el Espíritu Santo desciende sobre la casa de Cornelio y Pedro manda bautizarlos.

stem: In John 21, at breakfast by the Sea of Tiberias after the resurrection, what does Jesus ask Peter, how many times, and what does he tell him to do?
why: John 21:15–17: three times Jesus asks Simon Peter whether he loves him; each time Peter says yes, and Jesus answers, "Feed my lambs" or "Feed my sheep." Readers often link the three questions to Peter's three denials by the charcoal fire.

rubric.point: Says Jesus asks Peter whether he loves him, three times. Saying he asks once or twice counts as partly; saying he asks whether Peter believes in him does not count.
Says Jesus tells him to feed or tend his lambs or sheep (look after his people). 'Follow me' alone counts as partly.
Mentions the link to Peter's three denials, the charcoal fire, or Peter being grieved at the third question (optional, strengthens).

es.stem: En Juan 21, en el desayuno junto al mar de Tiberíades después de la resurrección, ¿qué le pregunta Jesús a Pedro, cuántas veces, y qué le dice que haga?
es.why: Juan 21:15–17: tres veces Jesús le pregunta a Simón Pedro si lo ama; cada vez Pedro dice que sí, y Jesús responde: "Apacienta mis corderos" o "Apacienta mis ovejas". Muchos lectores relacionan las tres preguntas con las tres negaciones de Pedro junto a la fogata.

stem: In Luke 24, two disciples walk to Emmaus with a stranger who is the risen Jesus. When and how do they finally recognize him?
why: Luke 24:28–35: they urge the stranger to stay, and at the table he takes bread, blesses it, breaks it and gives it to them; their eyes are opened, he vanishes, and they hurry back to Jerusalem to tell how he was known in the breaking of bread.

rubric.point: Says they recognize him at the meal in the village, when he takes, blesses and breaks the bread ("the breaking of bread"). Saying only 'at dinner' without the bread counts as partly.
Says they did not recognize him on the road, even while he explained the scriptures to them; or that their eyes were held and then opened.
Mentions that he vanishes from sight, that their hearts burned on the road, or that they return to Jerusalem that same hour (optional, strengthens).

es.stem: En Lucas 24, dos discípulos caminan hacia Emaús con un desconocido que es Jesús resucitado. ¿Cuándo y cómo lo reconocen por fin?
es.why: Lucas 24:28–35: le insisten al desconocido que se quede, y en la mesa él toma el pan, lo bendice, lo parte y se lo da; se les abren los ojos, él desaparece, y vuelven deprisa a Jerusalén a contar cómo lo reconocieron al partir el pan.
